https://www.grandprix.com/news/honda-say.text: AUGUST 4, 2026 Honda says strained Aston relationship better and better Honda says its relationship with Aston Martin, perceived early in 2026 as strained, has improved sharply as both sides prepare to combine the team's new chassis with an upgraded power unit at Zandvoort. The partnership endured a disastrous start to 2026, including severe engine vibrations, reliability failures and reported tension over how the Adrian Newey-led team and Honda should address the car's weaknesses. However, Aston Martin gained more than a second per lap with its heavily revised 'B' specification in Hungary, where Fernando Alonso reached Q2 for the first time this season and both cars recovered positions in the race. Our partnership with Aston Martin is getting better and better, Honda Racing Corporation president Koji Watanabe said while attending the Super GT round at Fuji. I think we're now in complete agreement on how to improve the overall performance of each car, what goals we should set, and what kinds of tests we should try to achieve that, he told as-web.jp. Honda's new specification engine completed its first track running during Aston Martin's filming day at the Hungaroring last week and will make its race debut after the summer break. For the next race in Zandvoort, the updates will be mainly focused on the power unit, but when we change something, we never develop only one side, said Watanabe. They always go together. In that sense, we want to make sure we get a good result for our next race in Zandvoort. Aston Martin ambassador Pedro de la Rosa agrees that the technical progress has been matched by a much healthier working relationship. Our communication has improved a lot, he told Automoto.it. The relationship with Honda has incredibly improved at all levels. We started without really knowing the people or the way they worked, with a new technical regulation that represented an additional challenge. Not having customer teams didn't help in this context. You have to know each other to work well. De la Rosa said the early reliability crisis ultimately forced both organisations to cooperate more effectively. We are very happy with how we managed very complex situations together, such as the one related to reliability. The difficulties in Bahrain, the first races we couldn't finish. But we remained united to find a solution. He said Hungary's successful chassis debut also confirmed that Aston Martin's simulation and correlation problems are being resolved. It shows that the simulation tools work and that the correlation with the wind tunnel and CFD is high. This wasn't the case in the past. It gives us confidence in our tools for future developments. However, De la Rosa would not predict how much the Honda upgrade will deliver, amid reported expectations ranging from a significant 30-50 horsepower. We have our expectations, but we haven't tried it in the simulator yet, he said. It's best to be cautious before making any predictions. (GMM)

The information they collect and share with ODIHR also contributes to ODIHR’s annual hate crime reporting. ODIHR is organizing a one-day training in Gdańsk, in co-operation with the Gdańsk Centre for Equal Treatment , to strengthen the ability of local civil society organizations to identify, record and report hate crimes using ODIHR’s methodology. The training builds on an introductory event held in Gdańsk in December 2022 and continued co-operation with the Gdańsk Centre for Equal Treatment on hate crime reporting. Objectives Participants will learn how to identify and record hate crimes, including how to recognize indicators of bias. They will discuss ODIHR’s definition of hate crime, the difference between hate crimes, other crimes and hate speech, and relevant Polish legislation. The training will also strengthen participants’ skills in monitoring and reporting hate crimes to ODIHR and in providing sensitive and respectful support to victims. Programme Through presentations, practical examples and exercises, participants will explore: the impact of hate crimes on victims and communities; the definition of hate crime and how it differs from other crimes and hate speech; bias motivation and bias indicators; monitoring, recording and reporting hate crimes; and sensitive and respectful approaches to supporting hate crime victims. Photograph: Dave Hunt/AAP Australia weather Thunderstorms, giant hail and powerful winds forecast for NSW as wild weather hits east coast Volatile weather predicted after storms on Saturday, with a man in his 20s struck by lightning while swimming on NSW Central Coast Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Stephanie Convery Sat 14 Nov 2026 20.52 EST Last modified on Sat 14 Nov 2026 20.54 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Dangerous and severe “supercell” thunderstorms with the potential for giant hail and destructive winds were forecast for parts of New South Wales on Sunday, as volatile weather continued in the eastern states over the weekend. Storms dumped heavy rain across large parts of northern and eastern NSW and much of Queensland on Saturday, with strong winds recorded up to 98km/h in Goulburn and rainfall totals of between 30mm and 50mm in the Coffs Harbour area. A man in his 20s was struck by lightning while swimming at Ettalong beach on NSW’s Central Coast on Saturday afternoon. He was pulled from the water by fellow swimmers and given CPR by first responders until NSW Ambulance paramedics arrived. He was taken to Gosford hospital in a serious condition, and later transferred to Royal North Shore hospital. The young man was in a critical but stable condition on Sunday morning, a hospital spokesperson said. Witnesses said while there was storm activity visible in the distance towards Gosford, the area around the beach was clear and sunny and that the lightning bolt appeared to come “out of nowhere”. Sign up for the Breaking News Australia email Lightning can strike up to 30km from the centre of a storm cell. Sunday was expected to be “another big storm day”, with “very dangerous and severe thunderstorms” likely for north-eastern NSW, said Sarah Scully, senior meteorologist at the Bureau of Meteorology. View image in fullscreen Authorities attend the scene after a man in his 20s was struck by lightning while swimming at Ettalong beach on the NSW Central Coast on Saturday. Photograph: 9 News Those storms could bring hail with a diameter greater than 5cm, and winds in excess of 120km/h. “That’s being driven by a southerly change that’s pushing up the New South Wales coast,” Scully said. “It’s a potential trigger for these supercell high-end thunderstorms.” Severe thunderstorms with 2cm hail, wind gusts in excess of 90km/h, heavy rainfall and flash flooding was possible on Sunday through a broader area of NSW extending down towards inland parts of the ranges to the east of Sydney, and pushing up into south-east and central parts of Queensland. Storms were expected in Sydney on Sunday, but were likely to be less severe than further north, though rain was likely. The forecast temperature was 23C. Showers and thunderstorms were expected in Brisbane with a top of 31C. The BoM expected to release more severe weather warnings throughout Sunday as the storms develop. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | When needed Sign up to Breaking News Australia Get the most important news as it breaks after newsletter promotion On Monday, the risk of high-end severe thunderstorms would move into the NSW northern rivers and south-eastern parts of Queensland, including Brisbane, the Gold Coast and the Sunshine Coast, again with the potential to bring giant hail, destructive winds, and intense rain that could lead to life-threatening flash flooding. “That again is being driven by that trough that’s pushing up the coast combined with the very humid conditions that eastern Australia has been experiencing the last few days,” Scully said. A coastal trough with a low-pressure system appeared to be developing off the north coast of NSW near the Queensland border, which had the potential to bring even more rain onto the coast. “How much rainfall accumulates is highly dependent on how close that trough sits to the coast, and also how long it lingers there,” Scully said. “At this state we’re only expecting moderate rainfall totals during tomorrow from that coastal trough, between 30mm to 70mm, easing into Tuesday morning. But we are watching it very closely as rainfall totals associated with these coastal troughs are notoriously challenging to predict. If they just move that little bit closer to the coast they can sometimes dump a whole lot of rain.” Elsewhere, there were showers developing in Melbourne on Sunday with a forecast top of 17C. There was a high chance of showers in Hobart, with 13C expected, and cloudy in Adelaide with a mild 20C forecast. It was partly cloudy in Canberra, where they were expecting 24C, and in Perth, with an expected top of 28C. Darwin was expecting 34C and an afternoon storm.
